Automating coherent long-form video generation
summary: Google introduced a multi-agent framework for generating coherent long-form videos, addressing identity drift and cascading failures in current pipelines. The system combines four components: Co-Director uses multi-armed bandits for creative strategy optimization, CANVAS maintains visual memory for character and scene consistency, A²RD generates minutes-long videos through adaptive extrapolation/interpolation, and VQQA performs closed-loop prompt refinement using VLM critiques. Built on Gemini and Veo with native SynthID watermarking, the framework treats video generation as global optimization rather than linear chaining, achieving 81.4 quality score on GenAD-Bench while eliminating manual intervention for temporal consistency.

Runway’s WorldPrompt and the Engineering of Real-Time Worlds
summary: Runway released GWM Worlds 2 with WorldPrompt, enabling real-time interactive 720p video and audio generation at 24fps. WorldPrompt lets developers specify worlds and timestamped actions, offering fine-grained control over characters and environments. The system uses autoregressive causal diffusion and step distillation to achieve real-time performance, though challenges remain: error accumulation in autoregressive generation, long-term memory limitations, and ensuring causally correct physics. Beyond gaming, applications include robotics simulation and agent testing at scale.

Accelerating vision-language models with LFM2.5-VL-DSpark
summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-VL-DSpark, a speculative decoding drafter for vision-language models that achieves 3.13x decode speedup on-device and 2.66x on H100 GPUs with only 280M added parameters (8.9% overhead). The drafter uses the same DSpark architecture as text models, operating on shared hidden-state representations across image and text modalities with a 4-layer attention-only design and block size of 8-9. For VLM builders, this enables significant inference acceleration with day-one support in llama.cpp, MLX-VLM, and SGLang. Key takeaway: speculative decoding gains are limited by Amdahl's law since vision encoding and prefill dominate end-to-end latency on edge devices, capping overall speedups despite large decode improvements.

Introducing NV-Reason-CT Open 3D CT VLM for Radiologist Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: NVIDIA released NV-Reason-CT, a vision-language model purpose-built for 3D CT analysis that generates structured diagnostic reports with radiologist-style chain-of-thought reasoning. Unlike general VLMs that treat CT slices independently, it uses a dedicated 3D ViT encoder processing full volumetric data (192³ voxels) with 3D MRoPE positional encoding to preserve spatial relationships across 300-600 slices. On CT-RATE benchmark, NV-Reason-CT achieves 0.614 macro-F1 and 0.871 macro-AUROC, outperforming all published baselines including VoxelFM and ClinFusion-8B. For builders, this matters because it enables auditable, conversational CT analysis with multiturn follow-up capability—critical for clinical integration. Key takeaway: native 3D processing with reasoning-trained language models beats slice-based approaches for volumetric medical imaging.

Watermarking in vLLM
summary: vLLM now supports Gumbel-max watermarking for LLM outputs, embedding provenance signals without distorting generation distributions. The technique uses pseudorandom functions to reproducibly add noise to token logits during sampling, allowing detectors with the secret key to verify authenticity. This matters because it enables content attribution while maintaining output quality and diversity. The implementation fuses GPU operations into a single kernel, achieving negligible overhead (−1.1% to +2.0% throughput change) and integrating with speculative decoding through dual-key schemes. Key takeaway: watermarking is now practical in production serving engines without sacrificing performance or output quality.
